Vendored AAA C# source — built from source in Linux CI (no prebuilt .exe/.dll)
===============================================================================

Upstream project : https://gitlab.com/wolfre/vhs-decode-auto-audio-align
Vendored version  : v1.0.2
Upstream commit    : 1790365e9561e6ab9cc8594cc560e76dc8da79a3
                    ("Merge branch '24-support-arm64-aarch64-appimage-builds' into 'main'")
Upstream tag date  : 2025-10-06
Upstream license   : BSD-3-Clause (see LICENSE in this directory)

Why this directory exists
-------------------------
The sibling directory ../vhs_decode_auto_audio_align/ ships the upstream
prebuilt Windows .NET assemblies (VhsDecodeAutoAudioAlign.exe + Binah.dll)
for the Windows and macOS builds (macOS runs them via host Mono).

This -src/ directory ships the C# SOURCE so the Linux CI build can compile
AAA from source and package it into a self-contained AppImage that bundles
the Mono runtime — which means the Linux bundle no longer requires host Mono
to be installed at runtime (the original "mono not found on Ubuntu" failure).

Build inputs
-------------
  - VhsDecodeAutoAudioAlign.sln            -- VS solution (main + test projects)
  - VhsDecodeAutoAudioAlign/               -- main project (.cs/.csproj/packages.config)
  - VhsDecodeAutoAudioAlign.Test/          -- NUnit test project (provenance; not built for runtime)
  - appimage/                               -- AppRun, desktop file, 256px icon (packaging assets)
  - nuget/Binah.2.0.4.nupkg                -- the single NuGet dependency, vendored so
                                              `nuget restore` uses a local source (no CI-time
                                              network fetch). SHA256:
                                              9D73C0223808ECDA52349E215CEB4584674A9F347AEF0FE48F976E9EC15E6B65

What is NOT here
-----------------
  - The upstream documentation images (*.png/*.drawio) and ci-*.sh scripts:
    not needed to build or package. See the upstream repo for those.
  - The NUnit / NSubstitute / NUnit.ConsoleRunner nupkgs (test-only deps):
    the runtime build compiles only VhsDecodeAutoAudioAlign/VhsDecodeAutoAudioAlign.csproj,
    not the .sln, so the test project's deps are not required. To build/run
    the tests, fetch those nupkgs separately.

How it is built (Linux CI)
---------------------------
scripts/build-aaa-linux.sh restores the Binah nupkg from the local nuget/
source, generates BuildInfo.cs with the tbc-tools build provenance, and runs
`msbuild VhsDecodeAutoAudioAlign/VhsDecodeAutoAudioAlign.csproj /p:Configuration=Release`,
producing build/VhsDecodeAutoAudioAlign.exe + Binah.dll. The Linux workflow
then packages those plus a bundled Mono runtime into a self-contained
vhs-decode-aaa.AppImage (replicating upstream's ci-build-appimage.sh approach
but using the distro Mono runtime) and places it at the vendor resolver path
expected by audioalignmentutil.cpp.

Updating
---------
To bump AAA: re-clone the upstream repo at the new tag, replace this
directory's contents (keep nuget/Binah.*.nupkg in sync with the version in
VhsDecodeAutoAudioAlign/packages.config), update this VENDOR_INFO.txt, and
re-run scripts/build-aaa-linux.sh to verify the build. The resolver,
bundle verifier, and CI contracts all key off the AppImage path, not the
version, so no contract changes are needed for a same-path bump.
